items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
Master's degree or PhD
4 - 7 years of related experience.

Delivers academic programs to students that enhance academic success through group, one-on-one, and course-based formats of service for a wide range of learning issues in a discipline for a broad scope of academic courses (e.g., lower-division writing across the curriculum; a cluster of biological science courses; lower division pre-professional trajectories in math/statistics). (30% time)
Assesses appropriate needs of students, and refers students to specific student programs. (20% time)
Collaborates with faculty, advising units, academic departments, and other student service units to assess students' needs. (15% time)
May provide guidance to student tutors. (10% time)
Applies and implements innovative academic support service models to support and enhance student learning, academic success, and intellectual development. (10% time)
Mentors undergraduates and graduate students to enhance intellectual and professional trajectories. (10% time)

Adapts counseling to specific learning styles and linguistic issues. Adapts consultations and instruction for students with diverse levels of methodological preparation—including those new to quantitative work as well as international and multilingual researchers—while providing accessible learning materials across multiple flexible formats, including live, recorded, and self-paced delivery. (5% time)
Read/Comprehend: Frequently
Write: Frequently
Perform Calculations: Frequently
Communicate Orally: Frequently
Reason & Analyze: Frequently
Bend: Occasionally
Sit: Frequently

Experienced knowledge of specific learning theory, learning styles, affective issues, academic issues, and socio-cultural/linguistic issues in applying academic support to students.
Proficiency utilizing data analytic software such as R, SPSS, SAS, etc.
Knowledge of how learning skills issues apply to a research institution.
Background in qualitative methods.
Knowledge of academic curricula.
Knowledge of survey tools and experience designing surveys
Knowledge in designing and implementing learning and pedagogical models.
Familiarity with FERPA and data privacy
Knowledge of strategies in critical thinking, reading, writing, note taking, test taking, time management, and goal setting.
Interpersonal skills.
Skills in judgment and decision-making.
Problem solving and organizational skills.
Knowledge of current research and theoretical models that influence the application and delivery of academic services (e.g., discipline specific, student-population specific).
Multicultural competencies, knowledge and experience working and interacting effectively with diverse groups of staff, faculty, and student populations.
Knowledge of program development, data gathering, assessment, and evaluation skills.
Proficient computer skills including databases, word processing, spreadsheets, and web-based systems.
Background in computer programming, such as Python and reproducible workflows such as Git, Quarto, and version control. Also, C++/HTML/Java with SQL or data visualization
Background in statistics, including but not limited to correlational designs, hypothesis testing, and ANOVA
Familiarity with AI-assisted coding and critical evaluation of AI-generated output
